# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jan 18 - 24, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism reached a major milestone with the successful rollout of Upgrade 18 across both test networks and the Mainnet, ensuring the Superchain remains synchronized and secure. Beyond this deployment, the team made significant strides in "under-the-hood" stability, drastically reducing developer wait times and resolving complex technical hurdles that ensure different parts of the ecosystem communicate reliably.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Expanding and Synchronizing the Superchain**
*Goal: To ensure all networks within our ecosystem are running on the latest, most secure version of our technology.*
*   Successfully deployed "Upgrade 18" to a wide range of networks including OP, Ink, Zora, and Uni on both Sepolia and Mainnet, maintaining parity across the ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1334)).
*   Introduced new blueprints for protocol upgrades and contract management to help developers launch and maintain their own chains more easily ([ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/874)).

**Boosting Developer Productivity**
*Goal: To make it faster and easier for engineers to build and test new features for the Optimism ecosystem.*
*   Reduced the time it takes to run network simulations from 30 minutes to under 60 seconds by fixing a bottleneck in how we talk to external data providers ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1351)).
*   Modernized our automated building system by moving to GitHub Actions, which simplifies how we package and deliver our software ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/532)).
*   Refactored the internal testing pipeline to only run tests on parts of the code that actually changed, saving significant time and resources ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18812)).

**Hardening Network Reliability and Security**
*Goal: To ensure the network remains stable even during unexpected technical glitches or high traffic.*
*   Improved how our software handles "resets" to ensure that if a node gets out of sync, it can safely return to a known good state without manual intervention ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18740)).
*   Updated our core execution engine to match the latest security and performance fixes from the main Ethereum project ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/751)).
*   Enhanced the "gateway" that manages network traffic by adding new validation tools to filter out bad data before it reaches the core system ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/539)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Client Interoperability**: A major coordinated effort took place across **design-docs**, **infra**, **op-geth**, and **docs** to fix "flaky" connections between different types of node software (`op-reth` and `op-geth`). This ensures that the Superchain remains "client-agnostic," meaning it doesn't rely on just one type of software to run.
*   **Supernode Reset Strategy**: Engineers from across the project collaborated on a shared strategy for how the "Supernode" (the brain of the Superchain) handles data resets. This involved deep technical alignment between the **ecosystem**, **superchain-registry**, and **optimism** teams to balance a quick fix with a long-term architectural upgrade.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jan 25 - 31, 2026)

This week, Optimism made significant strides in unifying its technical foundation by consolidating core Rust-based components into a single "monorepo" and formalizing how the Superchain handles network-wide upgrades. These efforts are designed to make the ecosystem more secure and easier for developers to navigate as we scale toward a multi-chain future.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was streamlining the Superchain's "brain"—the specifications and tools that manage how different chains talk to each other and stay up to date. By centralizing core code and defining clear rules for contract upgrades, we are reducing technical complexity and ensuring that the network remains stable even as we introduce advanced features like interoperability.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Standardizing Network Upgrades and Security**
*Goal: To ensure that as the Superchain grows, every chain can be upgraded safely and predictably without disrupting users.*
*   Introduced a comprehensive framework for L2 contract upgrades in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs), defining how the system manages its own evolution ([#881](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/881)).
*   Strengthened protocol security by adding a Failure Mode Analysis for the new configuration manager in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs), helping engineers anticipate and prevent potential system failures ([#364](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/364)).
*   Initiated a security rehearsal to test the removal of a signer from the Security Council in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops), ensuring our emergency response procedures are battle-tested ([#1359](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1359)).

**Improving the Developer and Operator Experience**
*Goal: To make it simpler for developers to build on Optimism and for operators to manage their own chains.*
*   Published a technical guide in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs) to help chain operators manage gas settings following recent network upgrades ([#1944](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1944)).
*   Converted several complex deployment scripts to "Forge" in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), which unifies the tools developers use and makes launching new features more reliable ([#18963](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18963)).
*   Clarified how different tokens are bridged in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs), making it easier for new projects to bring their assets into the ecosystem ([#1966](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1966)).

**Building the Foundation for Seamless Interoperability**
*Goal: To create a "Supernode" that allows different chains to verify each other's data instantly and securely.*
*   Reached a technical consensus on the "SyncStatus" API across multiple repositories, which will allow the network to monitor the health and synchronization of every chain in the Superchain simultaneously ([#18947](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18947)).
*   Implemented core safety filters for cross-chain interactions in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), a critical step toward making the Superchain feel like a single, unified network ([#18604](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18604)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
The week was defined by a massive "Upstreaming" effort to consolidate the project's code.
*   **Rust Monorepo Migration**: Several foundational libraries (like `op-alloy` and `op-reth`) were moved from separate locations into the main [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) repository. This coordination simplifies the build process and ensures that changes to one part of the system don't accidentally break another.
*   **Withdrawal Safety Coordination**: Teams across [specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs), [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), and [docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs) coordinated to delay certain technical upgrades to the withdrawal portal ([#18517](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18517)). This strategic pause ensures that users can continue to withdraw their funds without any risk of disruption during upcoming network transitions.

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (February 2026)

In February, Optimism focused on making it easier and cheaper for people to run the infrastructure that powers the network. By exploring new ways to handle data and tracking our own performance more closely, we are working to ensure the Superchain remains accessible to everyone, from large companies to independent developers.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this month was on lowering the "barrier to entry" for node operators by investigating high-performance execution features like Flashblocks. This initiative aims to reduce the heavy hardware and storage requirements currently needed to participate in the ecosystem, while new data-tracking efforts in our documentation ensure we are responding to community needs faster than ever.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Lowering Hardware Requirements for Network Participants**
*Goal: We want to make it cheaper and simpler for anyone to run an Optimism node without needing expensive, high-end hardware.*
*   The community and developers are collaborating on bringing "Flashblocks" support to the core software in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism). This would allow people to access network data efficiently without needing massive amounts of disk space ([#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/756)).
*   By focusing on these optimizations within the standard `op-geth` client, we are reducing the operational complexity for builders who previously had to rely on more resource-heavy alternative tools.

**Improving Support and Transparency for Developers**
*Goal: We want to ensure that developers building on Optimism get the help they need quickly and can easily find the right information.*
*   We launched a new performance tracking system in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs) to measure how quickly we answer questions and fix documentation errors ([#1967](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1967), [#1968](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1968)).
*   Active community discussions are helping shape the technical roadmap, ensuring that the tools we build match the real-world needs of the people using them.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This month saw a unified effort across the protocol and documentation teams to address infrastructure sustainability.
*   **Execution Layer Alignment**: Both the [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) and [docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs) repositories coordinated on the technical requirements for Flashblocks ([#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/756)). While the protocol team evaluated the code changes, the documentation team captured community feedback to ensure the final implementation solves the actual "pain points" reported by node operators, such as excessive disk usage.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Feb 1 - 7, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the "Superchain"—our network of interconnected blockchains—to ensure it remains fast, secure, and easy to manage as it grows. We made significant strides in automating how these chains stay in sync and began testing new "Flashblocks" technology to make transactions feel nearly instantaneous for users.

## Executive Summary
The overarching goal this week was to refine the "Supernode" architecture, the central brain that coordinates multiple chains, to prevent data errors and improve reliability. By resolving critical synchronization bugs and expanding our testing suites, we have cleared the path for more complex cross-chain features and a smoother experience for developers building on the OP Stack.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening the Superchain Foundation**
*Goal: To ensure that the many chains in our ecosystem can talk to each other reliably without falling out of sync.*
*   We improved the "Supernode" in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) by integrating it into our automated testing tools, ensuring that security proofs work correctly across the entire network.
*   A critical fix was applied to how nodes track the "head" of the network in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), preventing nodes from getting stuck on old data when using standard web connections.
*   We began designing the "SuperDisputeGame" in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs), which is a vital step toward a more decentralized and secure way to verify cross-chain transactions.

**Improving Speed and Efficiency for Users and Operators**
*Goal: To make transactions faster for users and reduce the high costs of running the infrastructure.*
*   Progress continued on "Flashblocks" support in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth), a feature designed to provide faster transaction confirmations while significantly reducing the digital storage space required by node operators.
*   We introduced new validation rules in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) to ensure these faster blocks are processed in the correct order, preventing technical glitches during high-traffic periods.

**Expanding the Ecosystem and Developer Experience**
*Goal: To make it easier for new chains to join the Superchain and for developers to build apps without errors.*
*   The Superchain Registry was updated in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry) to include "SaferSafes," enhancing security tools for both the Mainnet and test networks.
*   We added support for nine new chains, including Unichain and Worldchain, to our public-facing directories in [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io), reflecting the rapid growth of our ecosystem.
*   We identified and began fixing a discrepancy between different developer tools in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs) that was causing confusing "Block Not Found" errors during fund withdrawals.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This week required tight synchronization between our protocol, infrastructure, and documentation teams to ensure a unified rollout of Superchain features.
*   **Supernode Integration**: The development of the `op-supernode` required coordinated updates across [specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs), [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), and [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) to align on how "Safe" labels are managed, ensuring that all parts of the system agree on which transactions are finalized.
*   **Flashblocks Implementation**: Community-led efforts in [op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth) were paired with architectural reviews in [design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs) to ensure that faster block production doesn't compromise the protocol's core security invariants.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Feb 8 - 14, 2026)

This week, Optimism reached a major milestone in its technical evolution by consolidating its core software components into a single, unified "monorepo." This move significantly simplifies how developers build on the OP Stack while hardening the network's reliability through new failover protections and improved fee tracking.

## Executive Summary
The project successfully unified its Rust-based development environment, bringing together several key technical pieces to make the ecosystem easier to maintain and faster to upgrade. At the same time, leadership focused on "production readiness" by debating new ways to prevent network outages and refining how the system handles transaction fees to save users money.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Streamlining the Developer Experience**
*Goal: We want to make it as easy as possible for engineers to contribute to Optimism by reducing complexity and organizing our code better.*
*   Completed a massive reorganization of the project's "Rust" code in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19034), moving separate projects into one shared workspace for better consistency.
*   Ported over 60 pages of technical documentation into the core repository ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#18968](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18968)), ensuring builders have the most accurate information in one place.
*   Fixed build issues for developers using Windows in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/549), making the platform more accessible to a wider range of contributors.

**Hardening Network Reliability and Security**
*Goal: We are building infrastructure that is "always on" and protected against unexpected failures.*
*   Initiated a high-level strategic plan to support multiple "sequencer" endpoints ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#763](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/763)), which would allow the network to automatically switch to a backup if the main connection fails.
*   Implemented "Rewind Protection" in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19109) to prevent the system from accidentally overwriting finalized data, a critical safety feature for network stability.
*   Advanced the security modeling for the "L2 Chain Manager" ([ethereum-optimism/specs#18869](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18869)), using rigorous testing templates to identify and fix potential risks before they happen.

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
*Goal: We are growing the network of interoperable chains that share security and revenue.*
*   Launched new revenue-sharing tasks for the **Ink** and **Soneium** networks on the Sepolia testnet ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1369](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1369)), marking their continued integration into the Superchain.
*   Created a new "bulk signer" tool ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1368](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1368)) that allows administrators to update security permissions for multiple chains at once, significantly reducing manual work.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
The "Monorepo Migration" was a massive effort requiring synchronized changes across almost every part of the project. By unifying the Rust crates and Zepter configurations across [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), and [specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs), the team has created a "single source of truth." This ensures that a change made in one area—like a security update—automatically flows through to all other components, preventing bugs caused by mismatched versions.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Feb 15 - 21, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on making the Superchain more secure and easier to upgrade. By automating how we update the "smart contracts" that run our network and strengthening our connection to the broader Ethereum ecosystem, we are building a more reliable foundation for developers and users alike.

## Executive Summary
The team reached a major milestone by streamlining how the network handles upgrades, moving away from manual coding toward a more automated, flexible system. While expanding the Superchain with new partners, we also prioritized network health by investigating performance bottlenecks in our node software to ensure long-term stability.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Simplifying and Automating Network Upgrades**
*Goal: We want to make it faster and safer to improve the network without needing complex, manual technical work.*
*   The team introduced "batch upgrades" in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), allowing multiple network improvements to happen at once rather than one by one.
*   We changed how the network reads upgrade instructions in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) and [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs), using a standard data format (JSON) that makes the process more transparent and easier to manage.

**Hardening Security and Infrastructure**
*Goal: To ensure the Superchain remains a "fortress" for user funds and data.*
*   We successfully updated the digital keys (signer rotation) for our testing environments in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops), maintaining high governance standards.
*   The core engine of Optimism was updated in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth) to match the latest Ethereum standards, ensuring we benefit from the newest security and networking improvements.
*   We added new "checks and balances" to the consensus process in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth) to prevent the network from accepting invalid information.

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
*Goal: To grow the network of interoperable blockchains that share security and tools.*
*   We began the process of bringing "GNET by Galactica.com" into the ecosystem in [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io).
*   New tools for developers, specifically the Stork oracle for data feeds, were added to our official guides in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs).

**Improving Developer and Operator Experience**
*Goal: To make building and running nodes on Optimism faster and more reliable.*
*   Our automated testing system was upgraded in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) to run multiple tests at the same time, which will lead to faster bug fixes and updates.
*   Maintainers and node operators are collaborating closely to fix a "memory leak" (a bug that slows down computers over time) identified in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs) and [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Network Upgrade Transactions (NUTs)**: This week required tight coordination between [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs) and [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism). The specs team defined a leaner data format, while the engineering team implemented the logic to let the software read these new files. This ensures that every chain in the Superchain follows the same rules during an upgrade.
*   **Node Stability (op-reth)**: A significant effort is underway across [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs), and [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io) to diagnose a performance issue affecting archive nodes. This involves sharing data between node operators and developers to protect the health of the Base mainnet and other chains.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Mar 1 - 7, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the "Kona" technology stack and preparing the network for the upcoming **Glamsterdam** and **Holocene** upgrades. By resolving technical discrepancies and refining how the network handles data, the team is ensuring that the Superchain remains secure, consistent, and ready for future growth.

## Executive Summary
The primary goal this week was to align the new Kona verification system with existing network standards while proactively addressing gas pricing changes in the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade. These efforts ensure that as the Superchain scales, its security mechanisms—specifically fault proofs—remain accurate and cost-effective.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Network Security and Reliability**
*Goal: We want to ensure that every transaction on the Superchain is verified correctly and that the system can recover quickly from any network hiccups.*
*   Engineers fixed a critical issue in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19357) that helps the network stay in sync during "reorgs" (when the blockchain history shifts slightly), preventing data stalls.
*   The team refined the "Kona" pipeline in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs) to ensure it perfectly matches the standard OP Stack behavior, which is vital for maintaining a unified Superchain.
*   New security rules were added to [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19273) to automatically catch potential errors in smart contracts before they are deployed.

**Preparing for Major Network Upgrades**
*Goal: We are laying the groundwork for the "Glamsterdam" and "Holocene" upgrades to ensure a smooth transition for users and developers.*
*   Researchers began a high-priority investigation in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/19375) to adjust gas costs for the Glamsterdam upgrade, ensuring that security proofs don't become too expensive or break under new rules.
*   The "Holocene" upgrade specifications were refined in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/894) to give node operators clearer instructions on how to manage data storage efficiently.

**Improving Developer and Operator Experience**
*Goal: We are making it easier for builders to use our tools and for node operators to keep their systems running smoothly.*
*   To simplify the ecosystem, we officially announced the retirement of the older `op-geth` software in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1988), providing a clear path forward for users to migrate to modern tools.
*   We integrated new data sourcing options (Stork oracle) into the developer documentation in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1982), giving builders more tools to create complex applications.
*   Infrastructure efficiency was boosted in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/557) by optimizing our testing suites, which allows our developers to ship updates faster.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Kona Protocol Alignment**: A massive effort across **design-docs**, **optimism**, and **op-geth** focused on resolving technical mismatches in how data is parsed and verified. This ensures that the Kona "game type" (a core part of our security) is ready to become the new default.
*   **L2 Contracts Manager (L2CM) Safety**: Coordination between **ecosystem**, **infra**, and **optimism** led to new safety standards for managing contract upgrades. This prevents "storage collisions," a technical error that could accidentally lock administrators out of their own contracts.
*   **Glamsterdam Impact Analysis**: Teams across **superchain-ops**, **infra**, and **optimism** are working together to simulate how new gas pricing will affect the entire stack, from low-level code execution to high-level economic costs.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Mar 8 - 14, 2026)

This week, Optimism made a significant strategic leap toward a more secure and diverse "Superchain" by introducing zero-knowledge (ZK) technology into its core design. By laying the groundwork for ZK-based security and transitioning to a more modern Rust-based technical stack, the project is ensuring the network remains fast, safe, and ready for large-scale adoption.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was the formal introduction of Zero-Knowledge (ZK) dispute games, a major architectural shift that will enhance the security and speed of the Optimism ecosystem. Alongside this, the team successfully integrated the "Karst" network upgrade into the new Rust-based infrastructure, streamlining how the blockchain processes data and handles upgrades.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Advancing Protocol Security with Zero-Knowledge Technology**
*Goal: To make the network more secure and faster to finalize transactions by using advanced math (ZK proofs) to verify activity.*

*Goal: To transition the network's "engine" to the Rust programming language, which is known for being faster and more reliable.*

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Mar 15 - 21, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism achieved a major operational milestone by successfully modernizing its entire development build system and hardening the "Supernode" infrastructure that powers the Superchain. By resolving dozens of long-standing technical hurdles and refining how different chains talk to one another, the team has significantly cleared the path for more reliable cross-chain interactions and faster feature delivery.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening the Superchain’s Foundation**
*Goal: To ensure that the network of interconnected chains (the Superchain) remains consistent, secure, and synchronized.*
*   Refactored the **Supernode** to use a single, persistent model for cross-chain activities, ensuring that data remains consistent across the ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19505](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505)).
*   Improved how nodes verify data from Ethereum (L1), preventing state inconsistencies during complex cross-chain "interop" maneuvers ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19620](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19620)).
*   Corrected critical versioning for "Dispute Games" in the [superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1202), ensuring that the network's security rules are accurately applied to upcoming software releases.

**Modernizing Developer Tools and Infrastructure**
*Goal: To make it easier and faster for engineers to build, test, and deploy code by removing "flaky" automated tests and outdated build tools.*
*   Completed a massive, project-wide migration from "Makefiles" to "Justfiles," a move that streamlines how developers run commands and builds across nearly every repository ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19526](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19526)).
*   Resolved over 100 instances of "flaky" tests—automated checks that fail randomly—which significantly increases the speed and reliability of the development pipeline ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#18137](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18137)).
*   Optimized the "CI" (Continuous Integration) system by moving image builds to GitHub Actions, reducing redundant work and saving time during the coding process ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19603](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19603)).

**Advancing Future Proof Systems**
*Goal: To prepare the OP Stack for next-generation security features, including Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proofs.*
*   Initiated foundational work on ZK-based dispute games, signaling a strategic shift toward integrating zero-knowledge technology into the Optimism fault-proof ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19607](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19607)).
*   Proposed new mathematical functions specifically designed to support ZK dispute games in the [design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/369) repository.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Unified Build System Migration**: The transition from `make` to `just` was a massive coordinated effort involving [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19546), [op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/19546), [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19546), and [superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/19546). This ensures a consistent experience for developers regardless of which part of the stack they are working on.
*   **Test Suite Consolidation**: Teams began moving redundant tests from individual repositories into a shared "superfaultproofs" package ([ethereum-optimism/infra#19010](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19010)). This reduces maintenance work and ensures that security tests are applied uniformly across the Superchain.
*   **Ecosystem Troubleshooting**: Core developers collaborated closely with partners like **Base** and **World Chain** to investigate performance issues (like memory leaks) and "Bad Block" errors, ensuring that the software remains stable in high-traffic production environments ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#778](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/778)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Mar 22 - 28, 2026)

This week, Optimism made significant strides in securing the Superchain by finalizing the safety blueprints for Zero-Knowledge (ZK) technology and upgrading core infrastructure to the latest industry standards. We also successfully cleared a major backlog of testing hurdles, ensuring that the platform remains stable and reliable as we expand our cross-chain capabilities.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was "hardening" the ecosystem—making it more secure against attacks and more reliable for developers. We achieved this by integrating new ZK fault-proof specifications, migrating to more secure "hardened" server images, and resolving a series of persistent technical glitches in our automated testing suites.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Advancing Toward a More Secure, Multi-Proof Future**
*Goal: To increase the security of the Superchain by using multiple types of mathematical proofs to verify transactions.*
*   We introduced formal technical requirements and smart contract mechanics for ZK dispute games in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/896).
*   A comprehensive "Failure Mode Analysis" was completed in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/369), identifying 30 specific actions to protect the system from potential vulnerabilities.
*   The legacy "Optimistic" ZK game was replaced with a new, spec-compliant version in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19606), bringing us closer to a production-ready ZK proof system.

**Strengthening Infrastructure and Developer Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the tools and servers powering Optimism are modern, secure, and free of "flaky" errors that slow down development.*
*   The entire project was upgraded to Go 1.26 in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/579), ensuring we are using the fastest and most secure version of our primary programming language.
*   We migrated to "Hardened" Docker images in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/580), removing unnecessary software components to reduce the "attack surface" for hackers.
*   A major push to fix "flaky" tests resulted in the closure of several long-standing issues across [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19672) and [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/19586), meaning developers can now build and ship code with more confidence.

**Expanding Cross-Chain Interoperability**
*Goal: To make it easier for different blockchains in the Superchain to talk to each other and share assets seamlessly.*
*   We integrated essential bridge contracts for moving ETH between chains into the automated network upgrade path in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19648).
*   New testing tools were created in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/19726) that use real-world data to verify cross-chain communication without the long wait times of traditional tests.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This week required intense synchronization between our protocol, infrastructure, and security teams to resolve a critical "panic" (a type of software crash) affecting the **Kona guest program**.
*   **The Problem**: A missing piece of data in the "chain list" was causing the system to crash during proof generation.
*   **The Coordination**: This was identified and resolved through coordinated updates across [ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19654), [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19654), and [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19654).
*   **The Result**: The fix ensures that the Superchain registry can be read reliably, preventing crashes for users and developers interacting with the Cannon VM.

## ✅ Completed Work

### Fault Proof System & Dispute Game Enhancements
- All `op-e2e` fault proof tests were converted to use `CANNON_KONA` and `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` game types, utilizing `kona-host` instead of `op-program` in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19791](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19791)).
- The `depset` configuration is now passed to the `kona` super executor to enable detection of expired messages in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19849](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19849)).
- The issue regarding fixing host arguments in the Kona super executor for `op-challenger` was resolved, with the challenger runner now successfully running `kona-interop` in tests across `ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io` ([#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18287)), `ethereum-optimism/docs` ([#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18287)), `ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry` ([#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18287)), `ethereum-optimism/infra` ([#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18287)), and `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18287)).

### Core Protocol Stability & Correctness
- A pipeline initialization bug in `kona` using an incorrect system config during reset was fixed in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19792](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19792)).
- A new Semgrep rule was implemented to prevent `L2ContractsManager` from declaring storage variables, avoiding collisions in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19649](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19649)).
- The `L2Transactions` hint is now sent before the trie walk during block re-execution in `kona` in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19850](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19850)).
- Flaky tests `TestSupernodeInteropChainLag` and `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_DisabledReqRespSync` had their `MarkFlaky` tags removed after showing recent stability in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19846](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19846)).
- A specific flake in `eth_simulateV1` acceptance tests was resolved in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19842](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19842)).
- The proofs ExEx state provider was updated to error if state is unavailable, rather than falling back to a historical provider in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19855](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19855)).

### Infrastructure & Tokenomics Updates
- The circulating supply of OP tokens was updated from 2,117,847,344 to 2,136,461,507 in `ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io` ([#1297](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1297)).
- `proxyd` now tracks `safeBlockHash` and `finalizedBlockHash` in its consensus state, improving block hash fetching accuracy in `ethereum-optimism/infra` ([#591](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/591)).
- `proxyd` code was refactored to rename generic functions to EL-scoped names and extract a duplicated hash-verification walk-back loop into a reusable function, addressing type assertion panics in `ethereum-optimism/infra` ([#592](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/592), [#590](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/590)).
- Prestates for Kona client version 1.2.12 were added to `validation/standard/standard-prestates.toml` in `ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry` ([#1206](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1206)).

### Documentation & Build Process Refinements
- Documentation for historical proofs was enriched with context, architecture, metrics, and benchmarks in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19790](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19790)).
- The `nut-bundle-check` build process was simplified by replacing a Go script with a `git diff` approach in `ethereum-optimism/optimism` ([#19852](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19852)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Mar 29 - Apr 4, 2026)

This week, Optimism made significant strides in hardening the "Superchain"—our network of interoperable blockchains—by upgrading how we handle security disputes and cross-chain messages. We successfully transitioned to a more advanced "SuperDisputeGame" framework and cleared out dozens of technical hurdles that were slowing down our testing processes. These efforts ensure that as the ecosystem grows, the underlying technology remains stable, secure, and ready for high-volume use.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was "Interop Readiness," moving the protocol closer to a future where different blockchains can talk to each other instantly and securely. We achieved this by migrating to a new unified security model and resolving complex "flaky" tests that previously made our development pipeline unpredictable.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Protocol Security and Decentralization**
*Goal: To ensure the system can automatically settle disputes and protect user funds without relying on a single central party.*
*   We introduced a major architectural plan for a "shared dispute game," which simplifies how different chains in the ecosystem handle security challenges ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#370](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/370)).
*   The ecosystem officially began migrating to the `SuperDisputeGame` framework, a more flexible way to manage chain upgrades and security ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19253](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19253)).
*   We fixed a critical math error in the "Base Fee" calculation that could have caused the network to stall if it encountered malformed data ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#781](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/781)).

**Improving Reliability and Developer Speed**
*Goal: To make our automated testing so reliable that developers can ship new features faster and with more confidence.*
*   Engineers conducted a massive "cleanup" of the testing suite, fixing race conditions and "hangs" that were causing tests to fail randomly ([ethereum-optimism/infra#19805](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/19805), [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#19673](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/19673)).
*   We integrated new documentation for AI-assisted development tools like Claude Code to help new contributors get up to speed faster ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#783](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/783)).
*   The documentation team added seven new production RPC providers, giving developers more choices for connecting their apps to the network ([ethereum-optimism/docs#2008](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/2008)).

**Advancing Cross-Chain Interoperability**
*Goal: To allow users and assets to move between different blockchains in the Superchain seamlessly.*
*   We refined how the system handles "reorgs" (when a blockchain changes its recent history), deciding to drop certain pending messages to prioritize user safety over speed ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19814](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19814)).
*   The "Kona" fault-proof technology—a key piece of our security stack—was updated to version 1.2.12 and integrated into our core testing environments ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1206](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1206)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Fault Proof Evolution**: A coordinated effort across `optimism`, `infra`, and `docs` saw the migration of end-to-end tests to the new "Kona" stack. This involved updating how the software tracks data ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19803](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19803)) and ensuring the "Challenger" (the software that catches fraud) works correctly with these new tools ([ethereum-optimism/infra#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18287)).
*   **CI Stability Sweep**: Multiple repositories, including `specs`, `superchain-ops`, and `op-geth`, synchronized to close out dozens of "flaky test" issues. By sharing diagnostic data across teams, we confirmed that several long-standing bugs were finally resolved ([ethereum-optimism/specs#19661](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19661)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Apr 5 - 11, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on strengthening the "Superchain"—our network of interconnected blockchains—by making it more secure and reliable. We successfully updated our core technology to match the latest Ethereum standards and improved how our systems handle network hiccups, ensuring a smoother experience for developers and users alike.

## Executive Summary
The primary goal this week was to harden the infrastructure that allows different blockchains to talk to each other safely. We achieved this by integrating the latest Ethereum updates into our software and launching new "safety checks" that protect the network from invalid data.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Aligning with the Ethereum Ecosystem**
*Goal: To ensure Optimism remains fully compatible with the latest improvements and security standards of the broader Ethereum network.*
*   We successfully integrated the latest version of Geth (v1.17.2), the industry-standard software for Ethereum, into our core engine in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/782). This keeps our technology modern and secure.
*   New technical guides were created in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/901) to help our nodes better understand data coming from the Ethereum mainnet.

**Building a More Secure and Reliable Superchain**
*Goal: To make our network of chains more resilient to technical errors and more secure against potential attacks.*
*   We added a "Denylist" feature to our Supernode in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19880), which acts like a security filter to block suspicious data before it can cause issues.
*   We improved how our systems handle "reorgs" (when the network needs to reorganize its history) by using a more reliable data-saving method called Write-Ahead Logging in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19245).
*   A community researcher helped identify and start fixing a potential security vulnerability in our "Kona" technology, ensuring the system remains stable under pressure in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19334).

**Refining Economic Models and Developer Tools**
*Goal: To create fairer fee systems and make it easier for developers to build on our platform.*
*   We finalized the design for "Sequencer-Defined Metering" in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/360), which helps manage how much activity the network can handle at once.
*   We proposed a new way to handle transaction fees and rebates in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/361) to make costs more predictable.
*   To make things simpler for contributors, we moved all our technical documentation into one central home within the main [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/2019) repository.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Interoperability Testing Migration**: We began moving our "interop" tests (which check how chains talk to each other) from individual folders into a unified testing suite. This effort involved [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18974), [ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/18974), and [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18974) to ensure our cross-chain features are tested consistently across the entire project.
*   **Supernode SLA Standardization**: Teams coordinated across [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19180), [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19180), and [ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19180) to finalize the "Service Level Agreements" for our Supernodes, ensuring they meet high performance and security standards for the whole ecosystem.

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (April 2026)

In April 2026, Optimism focused on hardening the Superchain’s core infrastructure and streamlining the developer experience. By unifying technical documentation and resolving critical consensus risks on older chains, the project ensured that the ecosystem remains secure and easy to build on as it scales.

## Executive Summary
This month, the team successfully integrated the latest Ethereum standards into our core software while making major strides in cross-chain interoperability. We also launched a significant "housecleaning" effort to simplify our code and documentation, making the OP Stack faster, safer, and more accessible for developers worldwide.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Core Security and Ethereum Alignment**
*Goal: We aim to keep Optimism perfectly synced with Ethereum’s latest security and performance upgrades.*
*   The core execution engine was updated to match the latest Ethereum standards (Geth v1.17.2), ensuring our users benefit from the most recent global blockchain improvements in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth).
*   We identified and began fixing a "receipt root mismatch" bug that affected older chains, ensuring that even legacy parts of the ecosystem remain stable and accurate in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
*   New security rules were implemented to prevent accidental errors in how smart contracts manage data, protecting the network from potential vulnerabilities in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops).

**Advancing Seamless Cross-Chain Interoperability**
*Goal: We are building a "Superchain" where different networks can talk to each other as if they were one.*
*   We simplified the technical "blueprint" for how nodes communicate, making the system more efficient and easier for operators to run in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs).
*   The "Kona" fault-proof system—a critical piece of our security puzzle—was successfully tested for cross-chain use, bringing us closer to a fully decentralized Superchain in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry).
*   We reached a consensus on how to handle network reorganizations safely, prioritizing user security over complex technical workarounds in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs).

**Improving Developer Experience and System Efficiency**
*Goal: We want to make it as easy as possible for developers to build and maintain applications on Optimism.*
*   All technical documentation was moved into a single "monorepo" to provide a one-stop shop for builders, reducing confusion and speeding up development in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs).
*   We initiated a massive cleanup of our software "dependencies," removing over 100 unused pieces of code to make our systems lighter, faster to build, and more secure in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
*   New templates were introduced to help chain operators configure their networks more quickly and with fewer errors in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Interoperability Testing**: Multiple teams coordinated to migrate testing suites from individual repositories into a unified "acceptance test" framework. This ensures that changes in one part of the stack don't break the interoperability features in another.
*   **L1 Reorg Handling**: A coordinated effort across the `infra`, `docs`, and `optimism` repositories led to the implementation of "Write-Ahead Logging" (WAL). This technical fix ensures that all parts of the Superchain stay in sync even when the underlying Ethereum network experiences a temporary "hiccup" or reorganization.
*   **Monorepo Migration**: The project continued its strategic shift toward a monorepo structure, centralizing documentation, specifications, and core code to improve collaboration across different technical teams.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Apr 12 - 18, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the core infrastructure that powers the Superchain, specifically by streamlining how the network handles upgrades and improving the reliability of its node software. By consolidating technical tasks and modernizing build processes, the team has cleared significant technical debt, paving the way for safer and more efficient protocol evolutions.

## Executive Summary
The primary achievement this week was the completion of the "Network Upgrade Transaction" (NUT) bundle system, which simplifies how the network executes protocol changes. Alongside this, a major architectural cleanup of the Docker build pipeline and the Proxyd service has significantly improved the stability and maintainability of the entire OP Stack.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Simplifying Protocol Upgrades**
*Goal: To make it easier and safer to deploy network-wide updates without manual intervention.*
*   Completed the "NUT" bundle work for `op-node`, allowing the system to read and execute upgrade instructions directly from standardized JSON files ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem)).
*   Consolidated multiple development tracks for `kona-node` into a single roadmap, ensuring a more unified approach to managing Layer 2 chain upgrades ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops)).

**Strengthening Infrastructure Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the network remains online and performant even during high traffic or regional outages.*
*   Overhauled the consensus architecture for **Proxyd**, improving how the system communicates with Ethereum to ensure data remains accurate and consistent ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra)).
*   Engaged in a strategic architectural debate regarding "Sequencer Redundancy." The team is prioritizing the use of industry-standard tools (like Nginx or HAProxy) to handle failovers, ensuring the core code remains lean and maintainable ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth)).

**Preparing for Future Network Hardforks**
*Goal: To integrate the latest Ethereum improvements and Optimism-specific features into the protocol.*
*   Added foundational support for the upcoming **Osaka and Jovian** upgrades, including new technical "opcodes" and gas limit protections that keep the network secure ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).
*   Refined the "EL-Sync" process to fix long-standing user experience issues where nodes would occasionally struggle to find their place during initial synchronization ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Unified Build System**: A coordinated effort across nearly all repositories (Ecosystem, Infra, Superchain-ops, and Geth) migrated Docker build configurations to a centralized `images.json` system. This ensures that every piece of the Optimism stack is built using the same high standards and security checks.
*   **L2 Chain Management (L2CM)**: Development of the L2CM system required synchronized updates between the `optimism` core repository and the `superchain-ops` repository to ensure that new "Fault Proof" tests and upgrade mechanisms work seamlessly together.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Apr 19 - 25, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism focused on hardening the infrastructure for the Superchain, specifically by stabilizing interoperability features and streamlining the core codebase. The team made significant progress in transitioning to more modern execution clients and resolving technical hurdles that ensure different chains in the ecosystem can communicate reliably.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Cross-Chain Interoperability**
*Goal: To ensure that different blockchains within the Superchain can talk to each other seamlessly and securely.*
*   Finalized the technical rules (specifications) for how chains interact, moving from the design phase to stable implementation in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/905).
*   Fixed a critical "mismatch" error in the Kona system that could have caused chains to disagree on the state of shared messages ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20147)).
*   Added "cycle detection" to message graphs to prevent infinite loops in cross-chain communications ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20303)).

**Modernizing Core Infrastructure**
*Goal: To make the platform easier to maintain and more compatible with the broader Ethereum ecosystem.*
*   Began a major effort to decouple Optimism from custom versions of Ethereum software, moving toward standard "upstream" libraries to simplify future updates ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20257)).

**Improving Developer Experience and System Reliability**
*Goal: To create a more stable environment for builders by fixing "flaky" tests and automating manual tasks.*
*   Resolved several long-standing "flaky" tests that were causing unpredictable failures in the automated build system, improving the speed and reliability of new code reviews ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19934)).
*   Introduced new automation templates for managing Superchain operations, reducing the risk of human error during network upgrades ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1397)).

*   **Kona & Interop Stabilization**: Protocol, infrastructure, and ecosystem teams coordinated across [specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs), [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), and [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) to resolve output root mismatches and finalize the `CrossL2Inbox` deployment logic. This ensures that the "Interop" milestone remains on track for upcoming devnet launches.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Apr 26 - May 2, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the core infrastructure of the Superchain and preparing for the upcoming Karst hardfork. By resolving critical synchronization bugs and standardizing how network upgrades are managed, the team significantly improved the reliability and predictability of the ecosystem for both developers and node operators.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was the technical maturation of the Karst hardfork and the stabilization of the "Kona" Rust-based node. Key achievements included the finalization of automated upgrade processes and the resolution of long-standing testing failures, ensuring the Superchain remains secure and scalable as it adopts new Ethereum standards.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Hardening Protocol Reliability and Synchronization**
*Goal: To ensure that new chains can start up smoothly and that all nodes stay perfectly in sync during network reorganizations.*
*   Engineers identified and proposed a fix for a "fresh-start" bug where new chains would fail to recognize their starting point, ensuring smoother launches for new Superchain members ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs)).
*   The team moved toward a more robust "polling" method to fix intermittent test failures during chain reorganizations, which will lead to a more stable development environment ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).
*   New priority systems were added to the infrastructure layer to resolve data discrepancies between nodes, ensuring the network maintains a single, accurate source of truth ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra)).

**Streamlining Network Upgrades and Governance**
*Goal: To make protocol upgrades safer and more automated, reducing the risk of human error.*
*   The "Bundle Canonicalization" process was finalized, creating a standardized, automated way to handle complex network upgrades across the entire Superchain ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry)).
*   The `op-deployer` tool was expanded to support new types of "dispute games," which are essential for the security and decentralization of the network's fault-proof system ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).

**Aligning with Global Ethereum Standards**
*Goal: To ensure Optimism remains compatible with the latest advancements on the Ethereum mainnet.*
*   A new design proposal was initiated to integrate EIP-8130, signaling Optimism's commitment to staying at the forefront of Ethereum's evolving technical standards ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs)).
*   Technical constraints for the Karst execution engine were codified, optimizing how the network handles complex cryptographic proofs ([ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Kona Node Parity**: A major effort was made across `optimism`, `infra`, and `op-geth` to ensure the Rust-based "Kona" node behaves exactly like the standard Go-based node. This included fixing critical test crashes ([#19895](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19895)) and synchronizing how both versions handle the Karst hardfork.
*   **Superchain Registry Integration**: Updates to the `superchain-registry` (such as adding World Chain support) were immediately integrated into `op-geth` and `superchain-ops`, ensuring that all node software and operational tools are using the most current network configurations.
*   **Dependency Management**: The community and core teams coordinated on resolving trait conflicts in the `op-alloy` library, a foundational piece of code used across multiple repositories to interact with the blockchain.

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (May 2026)

In May 2026, the Optimism ecosystem focused on hardening the "Superchain"—our network of interoperable blockchains—to ensure it is stable, secure, and ready for high-volume use. While engineers tackled complex technical bugs related to database upgrades, significant progress was made in automating how different chains talk to each other and how we monitor the system for security threats.

## Executive Summary
This month was defined by a transition toward production-readiness for the Superchain's interoperability features. We successfully enabled key security and communication tools by default while aggressively troubleshooting a technical hurdle in our node software to ensure a smooth upgrade path for all network participants.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening the Superchain Infrastructure**
*Goal: To ensure the foundational technology powering our network is reliable and easy for operators to run.*
*   We integrated new performance tracking metrics into the `op-supernode` in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20443), allowing us to measure and improve how quickly the network verifies data.
*   The core registry was updated in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1409) to ensure all deployment tasks across the ecosystem are using the most current and accurate specifications.
*   We identified and began fixing a logic error in how the system calculates verification requirements in [ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20481), which is vital for maintaining the shared security of the Superchain.

**Advancing Cross-Chain Interoperability**
*Goal: To make it seamless and safe for users and developers to move assets and data between different chains.*
*   We enabled "Cannon Kona" and "L2CM" features by default in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20470), simplifying the setup for the next generation of interoperable blockchain proofs.
*   The "autorelay" system, which helps pass messages between chains, was upgraded in [ethereum-optimism/supersim](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/pull/421) with better retry logic to prevent messages from getting stuck during network congestion.

**Improving Security Monitoring and Transparency**
*Goal: To provide better tools for detecting and resolving disputes on the network.*
*   We confirmed that our monitoring tools can now track multiple types of security "games" simultaneously in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20476), reducing the amount of hardware and effort required for network validators to stay secure.
*   A new automated security scanning initiative was launched in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/379) to continuously check our code for vulnerabilities.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Unified Dispute Monitoring**: A coordinated effort across [ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem), [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), and [superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops) clarified that `op-dispute-mon` can interface with both standard and supernode RPCs. This ensures that as we move toward the Interop release, existing monitoring tools remain compatible with new node configurations.
*   **Upgrade Path Alignment**: Maintainers across several repositories, including [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/1412) and [superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/1412), synchronized on the "V700 vs V800" upgrade templates. This coordination ensures that smart contract upgrades are correctly mapped to the upcoming Interop release (Upgrade 20).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (May 3 - 9, 2026)

This week, Optimism made significant strides in hardening the "Superchain"—our network of interconnected blockchains. The team successfully completed high-pressure stress tests on our new cross-chain messaging system, proving it can handle heavy traffic reliably over a seven-day window. By clearing out old code and fixing critical synchronization bugs, we have paved the way for a faster, more secure, and more unified experience for developers and users across the ecosystem.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was the rigorous validation of "interoperability" (interop) features, ensuring that different chains in the Superchain can talk to each other without delays or errors. We confirmed that our systems scale efficiently under pressure and integrated new security tools to protect the network's future.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Cross-Chain Communication**
*Goal: To ensure that sending data and assets between different blockchains is fast, reliable, and can handle massive growth.*
*   Stress testing confirmed that our interoperability system can safely support a 7-day message window, allowing for more flexible cross-chain interactions ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem#15285](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/15285)).
*   We improved how the network handles "unfinalized" data, ensuring that even during rapid updates, the system remains accurate and consistent ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#19059](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19059)).

**Improving Developer Speed and Efficiency**
*Goal: To make it easier and faster for engineers to build and test new features for the Optimism ecosystem.*
*   We overhauled the "Kona" build process to work outside of complex container environments, significantly reducing the time developers spend waiting for code to compile ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem#19057](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19057)).
*   Standardized our automated "image builds," ensuring that the software running on our servers is consistent and easier to maintain ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem#1006](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/1006)).

**Enhancing Network Stability and Security**
*Goal: To prevent technical glitches from pausing the network and to protect user funds through advanced security measures.*
*   Resolved a critical "stalling" bug that caused nodes to get stuck when restarting, ensuring the network stays online and healthy ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#20464](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20464)).
*   Integrated ZK-Dispute Games into our management tools, moving us closer to a future where math-based proofs provide even stronger security for the Superchain ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1410](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1410)).
*   Successfully updated security keys on the Mainnet to maintain the highest standards of protocol safety ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1399](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1399)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This week required tight synchronization across nearly all major repositories to prepare for the upcoming Interoperability release.
*   **Unified Testing Framework**: We migrated critical tests from individual repositories into the central `op-supernode` and `op-acceptance-test` suites. This coordinated effort helped us find and fix a hidden bug in how the Supernode handles data ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#20370](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20370)).
*   **Protocol Cleanup**: Multiple repositories ([ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20309), [superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20309), [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20527)) worked together to remove the deprecated `ProtocolVersions` contract, simplifying the codebase across the entire stack.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (May 10 - 16, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, the Optimism ecosystem focused on hardening the "Superchain" infrastructure to ensure it can handle high-speed, cross-chain interactions with rock-solid reliability. By resolving deep-seated synchronization issues and finalizing the roadmap for the Interoperability Devnet, the team has cleared major hurdles for the next generation of seamless Ethereum scaling.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Network Reliability and Stability**
*Goal: We want to ensure that the network remains stable and predictable, even during complex technical events like chain reorganizations.*
*   Engineers conducted a massive "cleanup" of the testing suite in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs) and [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), identifying the root causes of intermittent failures that previously slowed down development.
*   Improved how the system handles database restarts and data synchronization in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), preventing potential data loss or service interruptions during maintenance.

**Advancing the Interoperable Superchain**
*Goal: We are building a future where multiple blockchains work together as one single, easy-to-use system.*
*   The team formalized the "Definition of Done" for the Interop Proofs Devnet in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry), setting clear milestones for cross-chain security and "flashblocks" (ultra-fast transactions).
*   Successfully completed stress testing on cross-chain messages in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), proving that our security model can scale effectively as the network grows.

**Streamlining the Developer and User Experience**
*Goal: We want to make it easier for developers to build on Optimism and for users to move their funds safely.*
*   Initiated a transition to "timestamp-based" withdrawal proofs in [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs), a change that makes the withdrawal process more reliable and aligns with broader industry standards.
*   Refined the "Optimism Contracts Manager" in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops) to automate complex network upgrades, reducing the risk of human error during governance events.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Standardizing Withdrawals**: A major coordinated effort took place across [design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs), [superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry), and the external **Viem** library. # Overall Project Weekly Summary (May 17 - 23, 2026)

This week, the Optimism ecosystem made significant strides in preparing for the "Interop" era, which will allow different Layer 2 chains to communicate more seamlessly. The team successfully activated a major technical upgrade (the Interop hard fork) in testing environments and shifted toward a more powerful "Supernode" architecture to improve how the network handles cross-chain data.

## Executive Summary
The project successfully reached a milestone by activating the Interop hard fork in core node software and resolving critical data-sharing discrepancies between different technical implementations. These efforts, combined with a major cleanup of the testing infrastructure, have cleared the path for more stable and scalable Superchain operations.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Cross-Chain Communication (Interop)**
*Goal: To create a "Superchain" where multiple blockchains can talk to each other as if they were one.*
*   Successfully activated the Interop hard fork using a new management tool, ensuring that different parts of the network stay in sync during major upgrades ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra)).
*   Simplified how developers interact with the network by reorganizing the "RPC namespaces," making it easier and clearer to request cross-chain information ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs)).
*   Began the transition to `op-supernode`, a more robust system for managing multiple chains simultaneously, which will eventually replace older, less efficient components ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).

**Ensuring Network Consistency and Security**
*Goal: To make sure that different software versions of Optimism always agree on the state of the blockchain.*
*   Fixed a critical "divergence" bug where two different versions of the software (Kona and op-node) disagreed on how to read compressed data, ensuring the network remains stable and unified ([ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs)).
*   Completed a "Failure Mode Analysis" for the upcoming Osaka upgrade, proactively mapping out potential risks and how to stop them before they happen ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs)).

**Improving Developer and Testing Infrastructure**
*Goal: To make the development process faster and more reliable by reducing "flaky" or inconsistent tests.*
*   Moved critical security tests to a more specialized "acceptance test" suite, which helps catch bugs earlier and keeps the main development pipeline moving quickly ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem)).
*   Identified and began fixing "race conditions" in the testing suite—situations where tests fail simply because of timing issues rather than actual code bugs ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Client Alignment**: Engineers across `op-geth`, `infra`, and `specs` coordinated to fix Brotli compression issues. This was vital because it ensured that the Rust-based and Go-based versions of our software process data identically, preventing network splits.
*   **Supernode Migration**: A synchronized effort across `optimism`, `design-docs`, and `superchain-ops` is underway to phase out the old "supervisor" component in favor of the new "supernode" architecture, impacting everything from documentation to deployment tools.
