# Overall Project Weekly Summary (May 24 - 30, 2026)

This week, the Optimism ecosystem focused on "hardening" the foundation of the Superchain by aggressively tackling technical debt and improving infrastructure security. While the team advanced next-generation designs for Zero-Knowledge proofs and predictive deployments, the primary success was a rigorous cleanup of the codebase to ensure long-term stability and reliability for developers and users alike.

## Executive Summary
The overarching goal this week was to transition from rapid feature development to a phase of high-intensity maintenance and security hardening. The team successfully streamlined the project's digital footprint through container optimizations and the removal of legacy components, while simultaneously initiating a deep-dive investigation into cross-client synchronization to ensure the Superchain remains resilient as it scales.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Hardening Infrastructure and Security**
*Goal: To make the platform more secure against attacks and more efficient to run.*
*   The project migrated core service images to "Chainguard" in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth) and [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), resulting in a smaller, more secure, and faster-loading environment for node operators.
*   A new "standby cluster" command was added to [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), allowing operators to safely set up backup environments without risking live network stability.
*   The community was alerted to security risks regarding the use of AI tools for debugging, protecting proprietary rollup configurations from potential data leaks.

**Improving Developer Experience and Tooling**
*Goal: To provide builders with more reliable tools and a clearer path for deploying applications.*
*   New proposals were introduced in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry) to support "Deployment Factories," which will help developers better track how their smart contracts are connected and deployed.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (May 31 - June 6, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism made significant strides in hardening the "Superchain" by successfully validating cross-chain withdrawal paths and finalizing the design for the upcoming "Osaka" and "Lagoon" upgrades. While the team reached major milestones in interoperability testing, they also proactively identified and began resolving technical hurdles related to system recovery and synchronization to ensure the network remains resilient as it scales.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Superchain Interoperability**
*Goal: To ensure that different blockchains in the ecosystem can talk to each other securely and recover quickly if something goes wrong.*
*   Successfully verified that users can move funds out of the network on a test environment, proving the core "withdrawal path" works as intended ([superchain-registry#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20489)).
*   Started building a "recovery runbook"—a step-by-step guide for operators to fix the network if it receives an invalid message, ensuring the system doesn't stay stuck ([specs#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21161)).
*   Proposed new "health gauges" to give developers better visibility into whether the system is running smoothly or needs a manual restart ([design-docs#21151](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21151)).

**Preparing for Major Network Upgrades**
*Goal: To keep the OP Stack aligned with the latest Ethereum standards and introduce new features.*
*   Finalized the technical blueprints for the "Osaka" upgrade on Layer 2, moving the project from the planning phase to active building ([specs#903](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/903)).
*   Began a coordinated effort to rename the Interop hardfork to "Lagoon" across all technical components to ensure clarity for the community and developers ([optimism#21129](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21129)).
*   Updated core internal tools to support the "Amsterdam" hardfork, ensuring Optimism remains compatible with the broader Ethereum ecosystem ([ecosystem#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/21069)).

**Improving Developer and Operator Tools**
*Goal: To make it easier and more reliable for developers to build and test their applications on Optimism.*
*   Transitioned from temporary testing environments to a "long-running devnet," providing a stable, permanent sandbox for developers to test complex features ([infra#20691](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20691)).
*   Optimized the "Docker" build process, making it faster and more reliable for developers to set up their local environments ([ecosystem#1007](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/1007)).
*   Introduced AI-assisted code reviews to help speed up the development process while maintaining high security standards ([optimism#21118](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21118)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Interoperability Recovery**: A major cross-team effort involving `specs`, `design-docs`, `infra`, and `op-geth` was launched to diagnose why certain components (like `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder`) require a full restart after a safety failure. This coordination is essential for creating a seamless "self-healing" network.
*   **Hardfork Alignment**: Developers across nearly all repositories coordinated on the `op-revm` synchronization strategy. By aligning these updates, the team ensures that every part of the OP Stack—from the registry to the execution layer—supports the same Ethereum standards simultaneously.

Today, Optimism significantly enhanced `op-reth` with new trie-state snapshotting for improved performance and integrated interop failsafe metrics, alongside critical bug fixes across core components and extensive CI/testing improvements. Key protocol specifications for post-execution transactions and Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM) were also defined, while `proxyd` received an additive `agreement` interop-validation strategy and a fix for CL backend initialization at network genesis. ## ✅ Completed Work

### op-reth Performance & Interoperability Enhancements
- Implemented a one-time trie-state snapshot feature in `op-reth` to improve read performance by allowing current-state lookups at an anchor block, reducing history-bitmap walks ([#20797](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20797)).
- Integrated the new trie-state snapshot into the backfill process, enabling reads from the snapshot during backfill and atomically advancing the snapshot anchor with each prepended block ([#20828](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20828)).
- Added a gauge metric to `op-reth`'s interop transaction pool to monitor the failsafe enabled state, refreshing on every failsafe poll ([#21151](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21151)).
- Introduced a dedicated JSON-RPC error code (`-320602`) for interop filter failsafe rejections, allowing clients to detect failsafe by code instead of string matching ([#21205](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21205)).
- Adjusted miner fee computation in the payload builder to use the pool transaction's `effective_tip_per_gas` before conversion to a consensus transaction ([#20382](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20382)).
- Resolved the issue of high cardinality for exported metrics in Kona, making metrics fetching more efficient ([#19927](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19927)).
- Fixed an issue where `op-reth`'s transaction pool failed to resume accepting interop transactions after the interop-filter failsafe was disabled ([#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21149)).

### Core Protocol & Infrastructure Stability
- Updated the withdrawal proving flow to support super-root dispute games by using L2 timestamps to locate matching L2 headers and selecting the latest usable game ([#21143](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21143)).
- Restored the `op-challenger` runtime image to Ubuntu from Wolfi to resolve issues with `cannon` binary execution due to dynamic linking dependencies ([#21236](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21236)).
- Corrected the `rollup-boost` Docker image to ship the actual binary instead of a cargo-chef stub, ensuring proper functionality with all dependencies ([#21233](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21233)).
- Fixed an issue where the `fork_lock.toml` validation failed due to the `interop` fork being renamed to `lagoon` but the lock entry remaining keyed as `[interop]` ([#21224](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21224)).
- Added a new additive `agreement` interop-validation strategy to `proxyd` for robust validation by fanning out `checkAccessList` requests to all configured supervisor URLs and combining verdicts by quorum agreement ([#640](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/640)).
- Fixed a bug in `proxyd`'s CL consensus mode, allowing CL backends to report block height `0` at network genesis ([#645](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/645)).
- Introduced new U19 templates for OPCM upgrades and mechanisms to set dispute game arguments and implementations, streamlining future upgrades and dispute game configurations ([#1448](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1448), [#1445](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1445)).
- Added a config-driven, per-slot storage-code whitelist to `MultisigTask`, enhancing flexibility during state diff verification ([#1450](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1450)).
- Defined new specifications for the `0x7D` Post-Execution Transaction envelope and version-1 Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM) payload schema, updating the glossary and protocol overview documents ([#908](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/908)).

### CI/CD & Testing Improvements

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (June 2026)

## Executive Summary
This month, Optimism reached a major turning point by officially transitioning to the **Lagoon** (formerly Interop) protocol and moving toward a more powerful execution engine. While successfully proving that cross-chain withdrawals work on our new infrastructure, the team also identified and began fixing deep-seated technical "deadlocks" to ensure the Superchain remains stable and fast as it grows.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Advancing the Superchain Interoperability Layer**
*Goal: To create a seamless experience where multiple blockchains work together as one unified network.*
*   Successfully proved that users can securely withdraw funds across different chains in a test environment, a foundational step for the Superchain's security ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20489)).
*   Renamed the "Interop" hardfork to **Lagoon**, aligning all technical parts of the ecosystem under a single, stable release candidate ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21105](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21105)).
*   Introduced "Safer Safes" to protect community funds with better recovery options and security locks ([ethereum-optimism/specs#914](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/914)).

**Hardening Infrastructure for Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the network stays online and recovers quickly from unexpected errors.*
*   Identified and developed fixes for a complex "deadlock" issue that was causing nodes to freeze during synchronization ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21076)).
*   Shifted from automated "experimental" fixes to human-led "runbooks" for complex network repairs, prioritizing safety and accuracy over speed during critical events ([ethereum-optimism/infra#20006](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20006)).
*   Implemented protocol-level limits on sequencer refunds to prevent potential "denial of service" attacks that could slow down the network ([ethereum-optimism/specs#20709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20709)).

**Modernizing the Developer and Operator Experience**
*Goal: To make it easier and faster for developers to build on and run Optimism nodes.*
*   Deprecated the older `op-geth` system in favor of the more modern `op-reth` for the latest protocol updates, streamlining the technology stack ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21188](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21188)).
*   Significantly reduced the time it takes to run automated tests by optimizing how the system starts up, helping developers catch bugs faster ([ethereum-optimism/specs#21191](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21191)).
*   Improved build reliability by fixing issues in our "container" system, ensuring that the software installs correctly every time ([ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#1324](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1324)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Lagoon Hardfork Alignment**: The transition to the Lagoon protocol required a massive, synchronized update across the registry, core protocol code, and documentation to ensure all chains in the Superchain stay in sync ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21105](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21105)).
*   **Execution Engine Migration**: The shift to `op-reth` involved coordinated work between the infrastructure, specs, and design teams to ensure the new engine could handle the complex requirements of the Superchain ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21069)).
*   **Upstream Collaboration**: Optimism engineers worked closely with the Paradigm team to fix low-level bugs in the `reth` engine, benefiting the broader Ethereum ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21076)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jun 7 - 13, 2026)

This week, Optimism reached a major milestone in its architectural evolution by completing the transition to a more modern, Rust-based system for securing the network. By streamlining our codebase and hardening the "dispute games" that protect the integrity of the Superchain, we have made the ecosystem more secure, modular, and ready for future growth.

## Executive Summary
The project successfully finalized the removal of legacy components to favor a more efficient and secure fault-proof system. At the same time, we made significant strides in "decoupling" our core technology from standard Ethereum software, allowing us to customize fee logic and cross-chain messaging specifically for the needs of the Superchain.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Modernizing Security and Fault Proofs**
*Goal: To move away from older, complex systems toward a more streamlined and secure way of proving that transactions are valid.*
*   The project completed the removal of the legacy `op-program` from the main codebase in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), officially shifting focus to the more modern `rust/kona` implementation.
*   Security was hardened in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops) by fixing a bug in how "dispute games" are deactivated, ensuring the system resets cleanly and prevents future errors.

**Building a Modular and Independent Protocol**
*Goal: To separate Optimism’s unique features from standard Ethereum code, making the system easier to maintain and upgrade.*
*   We launched a new "core" package to centralize how the network calculates fees and manages chain settings, reducing our dependence on external software in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
*   Technical specifications were updated in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs) to ensure that fee math is perfectly accurate, preventing the network from undercounting the costs of storing data.

**Enhancing Cross-Chain Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure that different chains in the Superchain can talk to each other safely and reliably.*
*   The "proxyd" service was updated in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) to include a "fail-closed" security default, meaning the system will stop a transaction if it cannot be 100% verified, rather than risking an error.
*   New tools were introduced in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) to allow developers to "smoke-test" messages as they travel between different chains, ensuring features like ETH bridging work as intended.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
**The "Geth Decoupling" Effort**
This week required intense coordination across **specs**, **infra**, and **optimism** to separate our unique fee-calculation logic from the standard Ethereum execution engine (Geth).
*   **Goal**: To create a standalone math library (`op-core/fees`) that works the same way across all our tools.
*   **Result**: By coordinating changes in the technical [specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs) with implementation in the [monorepo](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) and [infrastructure](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) tools, we ensured that transaction cost estimates remain accurate even as we move to a more modular architecture.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jun 14 - 20, 2026)

This week, Optimism made significant strides in preparing for the next generation of the Superchain by formalizing the "Lagoon" network upgrade and modernizing its testing infrastructure. The team also focused on "spring cleaning" across the ecosystem, resolving dozens of legacy issues to sharpen the project's focus on Zero-Knowledge (ZK) technology and protocol decentralization.

## Executive Summary
The overarching goal this week was to align the entire stack for the upcoming Lagoon hardfork while streamlining how we build and test Zero-Knowledge components. By renaming core protocol parameters and transitioning to more modern testing tools, we have cleared the path for faster, more reliable development of the Superchain.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Preparing for the Lagoon Network Upgrade**
_Goal: We are updating our core technology to support the "Lagoon" upgrade, which introduces better ways for different chains to talk to one another._
*   The team completed a full sweep of the codebase to rename and finalize the "Lagoon" hardfork parameters, ensuring all parts of the system are speaking the same language ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth)).
*   New testing tools were launched to help developers verify that bridges between different chains are working correctly under the new Lagoon rules ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).
*   We clarified the "warming" rules for the network, which ensures that the costs of using the blockchain remain fair and predictable for everyone ([ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs)).

**Building a Faster, More Modern Testing Foundation**
_Goal: We want to make it easier and faster for developers to test their code, which leads to fewer bugs and quicker feature releases._
*   The main testing suite was overhauled to use a more modern "execution engine," solving several technical hangs that were slowing down development ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).
*   We improved our "proxyd" service to ensure that different types of network connections (like WebSockets) are handled consistently, making the platform more stable for app developers ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra)).

**Advancing Zero-Knowledge (ZK) Technology**
_Goal: We are integrating ZK proofs to make the network more secure and eventually allow for much faster withdrawals._
*   The community reached a consensus on using "mock provers" for daily development. This allows us to test ZK features quickly and cheaply without needing massive computing power every time ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs)).
*   We began designing a new way for our tools to run ZK code, which will help us move toward a future where the network is even more decentralized ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This week required tight synchronization across nearly every part of the Optimism Collective to ensure the "Lagoon" transition and ZK roadmap stayed on track.
*   **Lagoon Alignment**: Changes to the Lagoon hardfork naming and logic were coordinated across [op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth), [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), and [specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs) to ensure a seamless upgrade path.
*   **ZK Task Centralization**: To improve efficiency, the team moved several ZK-related technical tasks from documentation and registry repositories into the core [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism) repository. This allows protocol engineers to work on these features in the same place the core code lives.
*   **Infrastructure Decoupling**: A major effort is underway to separate Optimism-specific code from standard Ethereum code. This involves coordinated design work in [design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs) and implementation in [op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth) and [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra).

## ✅ Completed Work
### Superchain Dispute Game Enhancements
- The `SuperZKDisputeGame` specification was introduced, detailing game mechanics, interfaces, and migration paths for zero-knowledge dispute games ([ethereum-optimism/specs#911](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/911)).
- The `ZKDisputeGame` was migrated to super-root semantics, mirroring `SuperFaultDisputeGame`, to improve dispute resolution within the Superchain ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21011](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21011)).
- The `nut` activation test was decoupled from the git head state for more robust testing ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21298](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21298)).
- Failure mode analysis for the `SuperZKDisputeGame` for interop superchains was added ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#381](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/381)).
- The design document for the Super ZK Dispute Game was updated to incorporate super roots and moved to a new proofs folder ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#384](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/384)).
- Issues related to `ZKDisputeGame` semantics, `extraData` layout, dynamic parsing, and `rootClaimByChainId` implementation were resolved, along with unit test coverage ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#20749](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20749), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#20750](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20750), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#20751](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20751), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#20752](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20752), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#20753](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20753)).

### Superchain Registry and Hardfork Management
- The Superchain Registry state is now coupled via a hoisted root submodule, ensuring a single canonical commit pin across `op-core/superchain`, `kona`, and `op-reth` ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21474](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21474)).
- The Interop hardfork has been officially renamed to Lagoon, with corresponding updates across the monorepo ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21370](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21370)).
- Issues related to coupling the `superchain-registry` state across `op-core`, `op-reth`, and `kona` were addressed ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21467](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21467)).

### Deployment and Documentation Improvements
- A new design document for Predictive Chain Deployments (PCD) was added, aiming to eliminate the 7-day permissioned window for new OP Stack chains ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#385](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/385)).
- The failure mode analysis document for the new deployment pipeline for Predictive Chain Deployments (PCD) was completed ([ethereum-optimism/design-docs#383](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/383)).
- The finalized Cantina security review for Interop L2 Contracts was added to documentation ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21472](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21472)).
- A note regarding permissioned fault proof chains was added to the Upgrade 19 (Karst) notice ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21484](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21484)).
- A developer workflow guide was added to the AGENTS documentation ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21480](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21480)).

### Issue Resolutions
- An issue regarding `op-challenger` requiring `cannon-prestate` in some permissioned game scenarios was closed with a workaround provided ([ethereum-optimism/specs#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21470), [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21470), [ethereum-optimism/design-docs#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21470), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21470)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jun 21 - 27, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism focused on strengthening the Superchain’s security and preparing for the next generation of "fault proof" technology. We successfully resolved gas fee issues following a recent network upgrade and made significant progress in integrating advanced zero-knowledge math to make the network even more secure and scalable.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Enhancing Network Security and Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the Superchain remains a safe and stable environment for users and developers.*
*   Updated security keys for the Foundation’s administrative accounts to maintain high-level protocol safety ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1479](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1479)).
*   Hardened the "Superchain Dependency Manager" through rigorous testing, ensuring that funds are correctly tracked and protected during complex transactions ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21502](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21502)).
*   Cleaned up the network registry by removing old test networks, making the system easier for developers to navigate ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1263)).

**Improving the User and Developer Experience**
*Goal: To fix technical glitches that make it difficult or expensive for people to use the network.*
*   Identified and fixed a "gas estimation" bug on the Sepolia testnet that was causing transactions to fail unnecessarily after the Karst upgrade ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1259](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1259)).
*   Began integrating solar energy tokens into the ecosystem, expanding the Superchain's reach into real-world green energy assets ([ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#1332](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1332)).

**Building Next-Generation Verification Technology**
*Goal: To use advanced "zero-knowledge" proofs to make the network faster and more decentralized.*
*   Reached a major milestone by integrating "kona-sp1," an experimental tool that uses advanced math to prove the network's state is correct without needing a central authority ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21489)).
*   Finalized the design for "Proof-Carrying Data" (PCD), a new way for different parts of the blockchain to share verified information efficiently ([ethereum-optimism/specs#921](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/921)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This week required tight synchronization across the entire stack to handle the aftermath of the **Karst Hardfork**.
*   **Gas Management:** Coordination between `superchain-registry`, `superchain-ops`, and `specs` was required to deploy configuration flags that fixed "intrinsic gas" errors reported by the community.
*   **Fault Proof Evolution:** The integration of the "Kona" project involved simultaneous updates to the core `optimism` monorepo, the technical `specs`, and the `superchain-registry` to ensure the new zero-knowledge verification tools work seamlessly with existing infrastructure.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jul 5 - 11, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, the Optimism ecosystem focused on stabilizing the network following the Karst upgrade and advancing the roadmap for Zero-Knowledge (ZK) security. By resolving critical gas calculation issues and streamlining testing infrastructure, the team ensured a smoother experience for developers and users across the Superchain.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Network Stability and Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the network remains predictable and cost-effective for users after major protocol upgrades.*
*   Resolved a critical bug on the Sepolia testnet that was causing "intrinsic gas" errors, restoring normal operations for app developers in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21457).
*   Corrected gas limit discrepancies on OP Mainnet and Soneium to ensure block space remains consistent with intended system settings in [ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1480).
*   Fixed a memory leak in the node software that could have caused system slowdowns during data synchronization in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21596).

**Advancing the Zero-Knowledge (ZK) Roadmap**
*Goal: To move toward a more secure and decentralized "Dispute Game" system using ZK technology.*
*   Reached a major milestone by completing the research and scoping phase for ZK Proofs in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21401).
*   Integrated "mock verifiers" into the deployment tools, allowing the team to test how ZK security will work on live chains in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21571).

**Optimizing Developer and Contributor Experience**
*Goal: To make the development process faster and more efficient by removing "noisy" or low-value automated tests.*
*   Conducted a strategic audit of the testing suite, deciding to replace slow, low-value "fuzzing" tests with faster, more reliable checks in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21636).
*   Improved the speed of cross-chain interaction checks, making it more efficient for apps to communicate across the Superchain in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/633).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
The week was defined by a highly synchronized response to the Karst hard fork.
*   **Unified Bug Response**: The "intrinsic gas" fix required coordinated updates across the execution client ([op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth)), the analytics engine ([op-analytics](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics)), and the core protocol ([optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)) to ensure all parts of the stack were aligned.
*   **Superchain Expansion**: Operational teams worked across the [superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops) and [superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry) repositories to migrate Ink Mainnet and adjust Osaka L2s, ensuring new chains inherit the latest security features.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jul 12 - 18, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism focused on streamlining the Superchain’s core technology by reducing dependencies on legacy systems and hardening security for fault proofs. By decoupling core infrastructure from older execution engines and expanding asset support on Base, the project is moving toward a more modular, secure, and developer-friendly ecosystem.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Modernizing the Developer Experience**
*Goal: We want to ensure that developers building on Optimism have the best tools and that those tools stay compatible with the broader Ethereum ecosystem.*
*   Coordinated updates to the `op-revm` engine to ensure upcoming support for "Glamsterdam" in popular tools like Hardhat 3 ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/21069)).
*   Introduced new monitoring metrics for node operators to track network upgrades in real-time, reducing the risk of synchronization failures ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21704](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21704)).
*   Simplified the deployment process by allowing the system to predict network addresses earlier, solving a major hurdle for launching new chains ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21560](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21560)).

**Hardening Protocol Security and Reliability**
*Goal: We are making the Superchain more resilient against attacks and more stable during high-traffic periods.*
*   Fixed three potential security vulnerabilities in the Kona fault proof stack to prevent unauthenticated attacks ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21713](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21713)).
*   Improved the "dispute game" logic—the system that catches errors or fraud—to ensure the network can finalize its state more efficiently ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#21708](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/21708)).
*   Transitioned to a more secure image-building process (APKO) for our software containers to ensure they are production-ready and tamper-proof ([ethereum-optimism/infra#668](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/668)).

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
*Goal: We are growing the variety of assets available to users and improving the tools used to manage them.*
*   Integrated new synthetic dollar assets (skUSD and kUSD) onto the Base network, providing more financial options for users ([ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#1337](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1337)).
*   Enhanced multisig wallet workflows, making it easier and safer for teams to rotate owners and manage high-stakes transactions ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1497](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1497)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Dispute Game Standardization**: A major effort spanned **op-geth**, **optimism**, **infra**, and **superchain-ops** to standardize the `IDisputeGame` interface. By adding a `closeGame()` method, the team is ensuring that all parts of the stack—from the execution engine to the challenger bots—can cleanly finalize disputes and update the network's state registry.
*   **Legacy Cleanup**: Multiple repositories (**optimism**, **infra**, and **superchain-registry**) coordinated to retire "pre-Regolith" testing suites. This shared effort reduces technical debt and allows the team to focus on modern, high-performance testing for the current Superchain architecture.

## Executive Summary
This week, the Optimism ecosystem reached a major architectural milestone by successfully decoupling core protocol services from the specific "Geth" execution engine. This shift makes the OP Stack more modular and flexible, while simultaneous efforts to harden security and improve documentation have prepared the network for upcoming mainnet migrations and more robust fault-proof systems.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Increasing System Flexibility and Modularity**
_Goal: We want to make the OP Stack more adaptable so it can work seamlessly with different types of Ethereum software._
*   The team finalized a massive project to separate core logic from specific software dependencies, making the system cleaner and easier to maintain across [ethereum-optimism/design-docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs) and [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
*   We simplified the "Superchain Registry" by removing outdated classification systems, reducing technical debt and making it easier for new chains to join the ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1292](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1292)).

**Hardening Infrastructure Security**
_Goal: We are committed to making our infrastructure as secure as possible against potential attacks._
*   All core service containers were moved to a more secure, "hardened" base image (Chainguard Wolfi), significantly reducing the potential attack surface for the entire network ([ethereum-optimism/infra#671](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/671)).
*   Core developers coordinated through secure, private channels to address sensitive technical edge cases in our proof systems, ensuring protocol safety remains a top priority ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#21344](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/21344)).

**Improving Developer and Operator Experience**
_Goal: We want to make it easier for builders to understand, deploy, and manage their own Layer 2 chains._
*   Launched a new automated system that keeps technical documentation perfectly in sync with the actual code, ensuring developers always have accurate instructions ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21873](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21873)).
*   Updated the "create-l2-rollup" tutorials and added new solution guides for custom deposit flows to help new partners get up and running faster ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21899](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21899)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **The `op-geth` Decoupling Milestone**: This was a massive coordinated effort across almost every repository (including `optimism`, `infra`, `superchain-ops`, and `design-docs`). By moving shared logic into a centralized "core" package, the team ensured that components like the "node" and "batcher" can now operate without being strictly tied to a single version of Ethereum software.
*   **Kona-First Fault Proofs**: Coordination between the protocol and infrastructure teams ensured that "Kona" (our new proof system) is now the default, with updated runbooks and testing tools deployed across the stack to support this transition.

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jul 26 - 1, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the "Superchain"—our network of interconnected blockchains—to ensure that adding new chains is seamless and that upgrades across the entire ecosystem are safe and consistent. By refining how smart contracts are deployed and managed, we are building a more reliable foundation for a scalable, interoperable Ethereum future.

## Executive Summary
The team successfully formalized the "Predictive Chain Deployment" framework, which standardizes how new networks join the Superchain. We also reached a consensus on a "safety-first" approach for protocol upgrades, ensuring that when one part of the network improves, all connected chains stay in sync without risking technical errors.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Streamlining Superchain Expansion**
*Goal: To make it easier and more predictable for developers to launch new chains within the Optimism ecosystem.*
*   Introduced the technical blueprint for Predictive Chain Deployments in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/921), creating a standardized "instruction manual" for new chain launches.
*   Improved the `op-deployer` tool in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22032) to make live deployments more resilient against network congestion and gas price spikes.

**Ensuring Safe and Consistent Upgrades**
*Goal: To guarantee that all chains sharing the same security features stay perfectly synchronized during software updates.*
*   Developed a strategy for "idempotent" upgrades in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21731), which ensures that shared components are updated across all chains simultaneously, preventing "partial" updates that could cause instability.
*   Refined how the system identifies administrative controllers during upgrades in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22034), ensuring that security permissions are handled correctly across the Superchain.

**Hardening Infrastructure and Security**
*Goal: To protect the network from vulnerabilities and improve our ability to monitor system health.*
*   Migrated core services to a more secure "Wolfi-based" image in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/675), significantly reducing the potential attack surface for our infrastructure.
*   Enhanced monitoring tools in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/676) to provide real-time data on service reliability, helping us catch and fix issues before they impact users.

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Interoperability Migration**: A major effort across `specs`, `optimism`, and `superchain-ops` focused on the **OPContractsManager (OPCM)**. This coordination ensures that as we move toward a more interoperable Superchain, the smart contracts governing these chains can be upgraded reliably without manual, error-prone interventions.
*   **Glamsterdam Hardfork Preparation**: Teams across `infra`, `superchain-ops`, and `superchain-registry` collaborated to analyze gas requirements for the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade ([#19380](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19380)). This ensures that the network remains stable and cost-effective for users after the next major protocol update.

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (August 2026)

Optimism is dedicated to building a scalable and secure home for the decentralized web. This month, our efforts focused on reinforcing the "foundations" of the Superchain—ensuring that the software running our network is more resilient to errors, expanding the variety of assets available to users, and hardening our infrastructure against security threats.

## Executive Summary
In August, the team prioritized protocol stability by tackling complex synchronization issues and improving how nodes recover from data gaps. We also continued to grow the Base ecosystem by integrating new tokens, ensuring the Superchain remains a versatile and secure environment for developers and users alike.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Network Reliability and Stability**
*Goal: We want to ensure that the nodes powering the network stay online and synchronized, even when unexpected data errors occur.*
*   We began improving how nodes recover missing proof history during startup in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), which prevents synchronization stalls and ensures a verified network state ([#22177](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22177)).
*   Engineers are actively diagnosing a complex "oscillation" bug in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) and [ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io) that affects how sequencers recover from chain forks ([#21964](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21964)). Resolving this is a high priority for maintaining consistent block finalization.

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
*Goal: To make the Superchain the best place for decentralized finance, we are constantly adding support for new and diverse assets.*
*   The Base network expanded its utility by adding support for **Wrapped Ratatoskr (wRATR)** ([#1346](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1346)) and the **WAKU token** ([#1345](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1345)).

**Hardening Infrastructure Security**
*Goal: We proactively update our underlying tools to protect the network from potential vulnerabilities.*
*   We updated critical networking libraries in [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) to address known security vulnerabilities, ensuring the communication layer remains robust ([#696](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/696), [#695](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/695)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This month required significant coordination between our protocol and infrastructure teams to address **Sequencer Recovery Stability**.
*   **The Goal:** To fix a bug where a node acting as both a sequencer and a follower would get "confused" during a network recovery, leading to a loop of resets.
*   **The Result:** By sharing logs and data across [ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra) and [ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io), developers identified that current height-based checks aren't enough to handle specific fork scenarios. This cross-team investigation is paving the way for a more robust fork-choice logic that will benefit the entire Superchain.

## Executive Summary
The project reached a major milestone in network security with the Kona SP1 proposer now capable of defending challenged games using advanced proofs. Simultaneously, the team executed critical ownership transfers for ecosystem partners and overhauled developer documentation to streamline the growth of the Superchain.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening Network Security and Fault Proofs**
*Goal: To ensure the Superchain remains secure and decentralized by improving how the system detects and resolves disputes.*
*   The Kona SP1 proposer can now defend challenged games using super-aggregation proofs, a vital step for the reliability of fault proofs ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22121](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22121)).
*   Introduced specialized monitoring "lanes" to better track and forecast different types of dispute games, including those involving zero-knowledge (ZK) technology ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22225](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22225)).

**Improving Infrastructure Reliability and Performance**
*Goal: To eliminate technical bottlenecks and resource waste, ensuring services stay online and responsive.*
*   Resolved persistent memory leaks in core monitoring tools that were causing services to crash over time ([ethereum-optimism/infra#694](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/694), [#685](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/685)).
*   Optimized the Jovian Data Availability accounting to be more efficient, reducing the "footprint" of transactions on the network ([ethereum-optimism/specs#926](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/926)).
*   Significantly reduced the time it takes for developers to test their code by optimizing the automated build pipelines ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22208](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22208)).

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
*Goal: To support the growth of partner chains and ensure they have the tools needed to launch and operate safely.*
*   Successfully managed the ownership transfer for Swell Mainnet and updated configurations for the Ink network ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1511](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1511)).
*   Advanced the rollout of the Superchain Dependency Manager (SDM) devnet, which will help different chains in the ecosystem work together more seamlessly ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#20176](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20176)).

**Enhancing Developer Experience**
*Goal: To make it easier for new builders to join the ecosystem through better tools and clearer information.*
*   Completed a major overhaul of the public documentation, making it easier to navigate and find technical resources ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22059](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22059)).
*   Improved the deployment tools to allow developers to resume interrupted network setups without starting from scratch ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21974](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21974)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Lagoon Protocol Upgrade**: Coordination across `specs` and `optimism` focused on adopting the "NUT bundle" to improve how different chains talk to each other and how data is stored efficiently.
*   **Node Stability & Sync**: Teams across `specs`, `infra`, and `superchain-registry` collaborated to troubleshoot synchronization issues between `op-node` and the `reth` backend, focusing on peering difficulties and integration test crashes ([ethereum-optimism/specs#20974](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20974), [#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20973)).
*   **CI Efficiency**: A unified strategy was adopted across all major repositories to prioritize smaller, incremental updates, which has successfully reduced the time developers spend waiting for automated checks to finish ([ethereum-optimism/specs#21186](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21186)).

- Refined Kona's engine and gossip protocols by moving signed gossip framing and SSZ codecs to private wire types, authenticating payload bytes before decoding, and introducing `OpExecutionPayloadEnvelope` ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22305](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22305), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22306](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22306), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22304](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22304)).

- Expanded acceptance tests for future L1 forks and hardened deposit gas accounting against upstream changes in `alloy-op-evm` and `kona` ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21920](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21920), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22372](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22372)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Aug 9 - 15, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism reached a major milestone in protocol efficiency with the successful stabilization of the State-Dependent Mining (SDM) test network, proving that we can significantly reduce costs for users without sacrificing performance. We also made substantial progress in automating how new chains are launched and began a strategic shift toward "Lightnodes" to prepare the Superchain for seamless cross-chain interoperability.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Reducing Costs and Improving Network Efficiency**
*Goal: We are testing new ways to handle data that make transactions cheaper for everyone in the ecosystem.*
*   Successfully verified that the new State-Dependent Mining (SDM) mechanism can reduce gas usage by over 50% for certain activities on the `sdm-net-0` testnet ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops)).
*   Deployed continuous "stress-test" workloads to ensure these cost-saving features remain stable under heavy use ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry)).
*   Integrated real-time monitoring dashboards to give developers clear visibility into how these efficiency gains impact the network ([ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io)).

**Simplifying Chain Deployment and Scaling**
*Goal: We want to make it as easy as possible for developers to launch their own secure chains within the Superchain.*
*   Completed a major phase of the "Permissionless Chain Deployment" project, automating the workflows needed to create and verify new networks ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).
*   Updated deployment tools to better estimate costs and automatically select the best security tools for new chains ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).

**Hardening Infrastructure for Interoperability**
*Goal: We are preparing our node software to handle a future where many chains talk to each other instantly and securely.*
*   Initiated a plan to move staging and production environments to "Lightnodes," a more efficient way to run the network that is essential for upcoming cross-chain features ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra)).
*   Resolved critical connectivity bugs in `op-reth` and `op-supernode` that were preventing nodes from staying synchronized with the network ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **SDM Operationalization**: This was a massive effort involving nearly every team. The protocol logic was refined in [optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism), the infrastructure was deployed via [infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra), performance was validated in [superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops), and the registry was updated in [superchain-registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry) to ensure the new testnet was accessible to all.
*   **Superchain Connectivity**: A coordinated fix for P2P (peer-to-peer) networking was applied across multiple repositories to ensure that different types of node software (like `op-reth`) can communicate reliably as the Superchain grows.

## ✅ Completed Work

### Infrastructure & Security Enhancements
*   **Ink SystemConfig Ownership Transfer**: Ownership of the Ink `SystemConfigProxy` was transferred from the Foundation Operations Safe to the Foundation Upgrade Safe on both Ink and Ink Sepolia networks, following a rollup-operator migration. ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1515](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1515))
*   **Security Dependency Updates**: Numerous dependency updates were performed across `infra` modules, including `click`, `@babel/core`, `google.golang.org/grpc`, `github.com/klauspost/compress`, `brace-expansion`, `golang.org/x/text`, `golang.org/x/net`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel`, `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9`, and `postcss`, to address potential vulnerabilities. ([ethereum-optimism/infra#690](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/690), [ethereum-optimism/infra#689](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/689), [ethereum-optimism/infra#688](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/688), [ethereum-optimism/infra#687](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/687), [ethereum-optimism/infra#695](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/695), [ethereum-optimism/infra#703](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/703), [ethereum-optimism/infra#701](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/701), [ethereum-optimism/infra#699](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/699), [ethereum-optimism/infra#698](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/698), [ethereum-optimism/infra#707](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/707))
*   **Automated Code Generation**: An automated code generation update modified the `addresses.json` file in `superchain-registry/superchain/extra`. ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1306](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1306))

### ZK Dispute Game & Fault Proof Refinements
*   **ZK Bond Accounting & Security**: ZK bond accounting was normalized to align with `ZKDisputeGame.sol` records, and complete ZK snapshots are now routed through all bond consumers. Security was enhanced by checking registered dispute game implementation identities and binding `AnchorStateRegistry` to the portal. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22228](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22228), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22365](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22365), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22412](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22412))
*   **SuperPermissionedDisputeGame ETH Prevention**: `msg.value` is now rejected in `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` initialization to prevent trapped ETH. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22410](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22410))

### Kona SP1 Proposer & Interoperability Improvements
*   **Kona SP1 Proposer Environment Variables**: `kona-sp1-proposer` environment variables were standardized with prefixed configuration styles. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22411](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22411))
*   **Superroot RPC Fallover**: Fallover for superroot RPCs was implemented in `kona-sp1-proposer` to prevent proposal stalls. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22416](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22416))
*   **Kona Interoperability**: Chains without explicit interop configuration now default to a self-only dependency set, and super-root acceptance coverage was expanded. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22408](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22408), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22392](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22392))

### SDM Post-Execution & EVM Stability
*   **SDM Post-Execution Transactions**: Zero DA footprint is now reported on PostExec receipts, post-exec transaction results are synthesized on replay paths to fix `debug_traceBlockByNumber` failures, and SDM post-exec refunds are applied exactly once. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22220](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22220), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22374](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22374), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22399](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22399))

### Testing & Infrastructure Stability
*   **`op-deployer` Test Isolation**: `apply` subtest deadlines in `op-deployer` were isolated to prevent cumulative budget issues. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22389](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22389))
*   **`txmgr` Queued Failure Ordering**: Queued failure ordering in `txmgr` was stabilized. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22388](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22388))
*   **Repository Streamlining**: Vestigial Docker files and scripts were removed from the `optimism` repository. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22375](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22375))
*   **CI Fix**: A CI fix was implemented to avoid SIGPIPE errors in the super-aggregation vkey gate. ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22415](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22415))

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Aug 16 - 22, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the core infrastructure of the Superchain and advancing its next-generation Rust-based technology. By successfully validating major performance upgrades and resolving long-standing networking bugs, the project has cleared the path for a more stable and scalable ecosystem for both developers and users.

## Executive Summary
The team reached a major milestone by confirming that new data management features (SDM) significantly reduce costs without impacting system performance. Simultaneously, the launch of "Lokahi" marks a strategic shift toward a more modular, multi-chain future using the Rust programming language.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Improving Network Stability and Performance**
*Goal: We want to ensure that the Superchain is fast, reliable, and cost-effective for everyone.*
*   **Validated Cost Savings:** Extensive testing confirmed that the State Diff Merkle (SDM) feature saves over 60% on certain data costs while maintaining a "neutral" impact on system resources ([ethereum-optimism/specs#20176](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20176)).
*   **Fixed Connection Issues:** Engineers resolved a persistent "flakiness" issue that prevented different types of software (Geth and Reth) from talking to each other reliably, ensuring a more cohesive network ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#18570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/18570)).
*   **Smoother Infrastructure:** Updated the internal tools that run our tests to be more resilient against temporary internet hiccups, leading to faster development cycles ([ethereum-optimism/infra#716](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/716)).

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
*Goal: We are building a network of interoperable chains that share security and tools.*
*   **New Chain Integration:** Began the process of adding the "Plataberget" network to the official registry, expanding the reach of the Superchain ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1309](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1309)).
*   **Asset Visibility:** Updated the token registry to include new assets like AI.DADDY on Base, ensuring users have accurate information about available tokens ([ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#1349](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1349)).
*   **Governance Readiness:** Conducted "fire drills" for managing security signers to ensure the network can respond quickly to governance updates ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1524](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1524)).

**Advancing the Rust-Based Stack**
*Goal: We are building high-performance, modular tools to make the OP Stack more flexible.*
*   **Lokahi Launch:** Officially rebranded and began building "Lokahi," a new tool designed to handle multiple chains simultaneously using the Rust language ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22509](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22509)).
*   **Protocol Integrity:** Implemented new validation checks to ensure that data moving between different parts of the system is accurate and secure ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22215](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22215)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Multi-Client Interoperability**: A coordinated effort across `superchain-ops`, `infra`, `op-geth`, and `optimism` finally resolved a long-standing P2P networking bug ([#18570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18570)). By normalizing how different software versions identify each other, the team re-enabled full verification for the entire ecosystem's testing suite.
*   **SDM Performance Validation**: The `specs`, `infra`, and `optimism` teams collaborated on a massive benchmarking project. This cross-functional effort proved that the new State Diff Management system is production-ready, offering significant gas savings without increasing CPU or memory usage.

*   Initiated a transition to a new "subblocks" framework to support faster transaction confirmations in the future ([#929](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/929)).

### ethereum-optimism/infra
*   Migrated core testing images to "Wolfi" to reduce security vulnerabilities and make the images smaller and faster ([#717](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/717)).

### ethereum-optimism/op-geth
*   Started upgrading the networking stack (STUN) to a newer version to help nodes find each other more easily behind firewalls ([#807](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/807)).
*   Investigated a synchronization bottleneck in the storage proof engine that was causing tests to stall ([#20376](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20376)).

Optimism's development today centered on significant advancements in the Lokahi interop project, including the implementation of multi-chain L1 watchers, robust storage solutions, and refined message validity rules, alongside critical security updates and infrastructure enhancements like the Rust port of `op-node SafeDB`. A major cross-cutting effort involved the removal of the "cross-unsafe" chain-head notion from Go components, streamlining the codebase and interop design.

## ✅ Completed Work

### Core Infrastructure & Interoperability Enhancements
- **Rust Port of SafeDB**: The `op-node SafeDB` was ported to Rust as `kona-safedb`, providing a 1-to-1 functional equivalent for tracking L2 safe heads per L1 block, crucial for fault proofs and interop systems ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21522](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21522)).
- **Configurable AltDA Input Limits**: The AltDA input size limit was made configurable, allowing operators to adjust it for Keccak derivation and batcher validation, ensuring alignment with Kona strict config parsing ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22496](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22496)).
- **ZK Challenge Support in op-challenger**: The `op-challenger move --attack` command now supports ZK challenges by detecting the on-chain game type before constructing transactions ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22575](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22575)).
- **Lokahi Interop Stores Implementation**: The foundational `lokahi-interop` crate was implemented, incorporating verified, log, and invalidated-output archive stores using RocksDB for persistence and binary encoding ([ethereum-optimism/infra#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22535), [ethereum-optimism/specs#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22535), [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/22535), [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22535)).
- **Lokahi Verification Round Loop**: The verification round loop was implemented in `lokahi-interop`, observing chains and L1, making decisions, writing to a WAL, and applying changes ([ethereum-optimism/infra#22536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22536), [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#22536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/22536), [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#22536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22536)).

### Security & Dependency Management
- **`libp2p` and `golang.org/x/mod` Updates**: Critical security vulnerabilities were addressed by updating `libp2p` to v0.49.0 (including `quic-go` v0.60.0 and `webtransport-go` v0.11.1) and `golang.org/x/mod` to v0.40.0 across multiple services ([ethereum-optimism/infra#724](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/724), [ethereum-optimism/infra#723](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/723)).
- **Security Review Publication**: The final Cantina security review report for Upgrade 20 was added to the documentation, providing transparency on protocol security ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22559](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22559)).

### Developer Experience & Protocol Refinements
- **Enhanced Developer Workflow Documentation**: New guidelines were added to `AGENTS.md`, requiring agents to watch CI after pushing to a PR and to run local review-agent passes before opening a PR, aiming to improve code quality and reduce CI failures ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22574](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22574), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22572](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22572)).
- **Go Code Reviewer Agent**: A new `go-code-reviewer` agent was added to Claude, mirroring the existing Rust reviewer, to enforce consistent code quality and style for Go contributions ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22561](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22561)).
- **SDM Testing Refinement**: Public warming production in Sequencer Defined Metering (SDM) was replaced with a test fixture, retaining mechanism coverage while maintaining derivation, stock-verifier, replay/accounting, and fault-proof coverage ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22222](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22222)).
- **Dispute Game Config Validation**: The `OPContractsManagerMigrator.migrate()` function was updated to validate dispute game configurations, preventing the registration of `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` games without proper checks ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22441](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22441)).
- **Removal of Cross-Unsafe Chain-Head Notion**: The `cross-unsafe` chain-head notion was removed from `op-node`, `op-service`, and `op-devstack` across multiple repositories, as it was an `op-supervisor-era` vestige no longer relevant to the current interop design ([ethereum-optimism/infra#22550](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22550), [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22555](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22555), [ethereum-optimism/specs#22550](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22550), [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#22550](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/22550), [ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#22550](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22550)).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Aug 23 - 29, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on streamlining the Superchain ecosystem by cleaning up legacy code and hardening the core technology that powers our network. We made significant strides in decentralizing chain ownership and improving the reliability of our cross-chain communication tools, ensuring a more stable and professional experience for both developers and users.

## Executive Summary
The primary focus this week was a major "spring cleaning" of the Superchain ecosystem, consolidating developer resources and archiving abandoned projects to reduce confusion. Simultaneously, we successfully transitioned the ownership of several major chains to independent operators, marking a significant milestone in our journey toward a decentralized Superchain.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Simplifying the Developer Experience**
*Goal: We want to make it as easy as possible for new builders to join the Optimism ecosystem by providing clear, up-to-date resources.*
*   Initiated a major consolidation of "starter" repositories into a single, high-quality entry point to reduce fragmentation across the ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/infra#1015](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/1015)).
*   Completed a comprehensive audit to archive obsolete tools and repositories, ensuring that public documentation only points to supported and secure code ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem#1014](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1014)).
*   Updated the Superchain Registry to reflect the addition of "Main's World" to the World Chain, keeping our ecosystem map accurate as new partners join ([ethereum-optimism.github.io#1356](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1356)).

**Advancing Decentralization and Governance**
*Goal: To build a resilient network, we are transferring control of key infrastructure to community partners and improving our deployment tools.*
*   Successfully handed over ownership of the Metal, Mode, Zora, and Dust chains to Conduit, demonstrating our ability to transition chain management to independent operators ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1521](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1521)).
*   Enhanced our ownership transfer tools to allow multiple security updates to happen in a single step, making governance more efficient ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1519](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1519)).
*   Validated the full lifecycle of a new chain deployment on the Plataberget testnet, proving that our automated deployment tools are ready for the next generation of L2s ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#22696](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/22696)).

**Hardening Protocol Security and Reliability**
*Goal: We are identifying and fixing complex technical bugs to ensure the network remains stable even under heavy load or unexpected errors.*
*   Modernized the networking stack in `op-geth` to improve how nodes find and talk to each other, reducing the risk of connection drops ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#807](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/807)).
*   Introduced new monitoring tools to track how long it takes for transactions to be included in the blockchain, giving us better data on the actual user experience ([ethereum-optimism/infra#726](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/726)).
*   Identified and began fixing a critical "looping" issue in the Kona sequencer that could cause high CPU usage during network reorganizations ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#22681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22681)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Superchain Starter Consolidation**: This effort spanned `infra`, `ecosystem`, `specs`, and `superchain-ops`. By auditing links across all these areas, the team ensured that merging five different "starter" repos into one would not break existing tutorials or developer workflows.
*   **Kona Protocol Hardening**: Coordination between the `optimism` monorepo and `specs` was vital this week to address sequencer stability. While engineers worked on code fixes for P2P stalling ([ethereum-optimism/specs#22646](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22646)), they simultaneously updated the protocol rules to ensure these fixes align with our long-term interoperability goals.
